messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: kv_cache.metadata_bytes rate increased 9.3x in prod-us-west-2 over last 10m. Error budget burn rising. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/kvcache/metadata-growth

mina: I’m on it. seeing big continuous-batching queue depth on block-manager nodes. paging/memory pressure across several pods. tagging eng-runtime and eng-sre.

rob: looking now — sounds like the new batching heuristic from yesterday is letting tiny requests accumulate into huge KV blocks. I can push a temporary reduction to the continuous_batch_size if needed.

mina: do it. set continuous_batch_size -> 8 for all blockmgr instances in prod-us-west-2. also bump eviction aggressiveness to avoid metadata blowup.

rob: doing the change now. patch command: ```kubectl -n inference patch configmap blockmgr-config -p '{"data":{"continuous_batch_size":"8","eviction_multiplier":"1.5"}}' && kubectl rollout restart deploy/block-manager -n inference```

carla: heads up — Auto-eviction is currently LRU with a 12h grace. Suggest reducing grace to 1h for critical nodes while we triage.

srikar: I can run an immediate manual eviction on the hot pods to free metadata. rob — which nodes show highest metadata_bytes?

rob: node-ima-4 and node-ima-7. manual eviction script: ```curl -X POST http://blockmgr.node-ima-4.internal/evict?policy=aggressive && curl -X POST http://blockmgr.node-ima-7.internal/evict?policy=aggressive```

srikar: ran eviction on both. metadata_bytes dropped ~40% on node-ima-4, ~35% on node-ima-7. CPU spiked briefly but falling.

mina: good. can we confirm downstream latency/customer impact?

carla: looking at customer-facing APIs: 5% of production requests saw >1.2s tail on generation tokens in the last 15m, mostly in us-west. A handful of B2B customers saw retries increase. No major errors 5xx spike though.

mina: OK — customer impact limited but measurable. open a customer incident note and notify CSMs for the affected tenants. @carla can you do that? include mitigation steps and ETA for full fix.

carla: on it. sending update to CSMs now. summary: temporary config change + manual evictions applied, monitoring closely.

rob: after reducing batch size and evict, metadata growth rate flattened. rolling restart completed on all blockmgr pods at 1719823800.

incident-bot: Deploy bot: rollout/block-manager v2.7.4 -> v2.7.4 (config patch) succeeded for inference namespace (12 pods).

mina: next: root cause analysis — initial hypothesis: the heuristic change in scheduler v2.7.4 caused prolonged prefix accumulation that prevented KV blocks from being flushed; combined with LRU grace window that kept stale metadata alive. we should rollback the scheduler heuristic change and add a safety guard on batch accumulation.

rob: I already created a rollback PR and a safety guard for max_prefix_aggregate_size. PR: https://github.com/redwood/block-manager/pull/542 - rolling it out after we confirm stability metrics for 30m.

srikar: will add a canary that enforces max_prefix_aggregate_size=1MB per-batch and a hard stop to prevent >8k keys per block. Adding unit/regression tests too.

carla: metrics now: kv_cache.metadata_bytes 10m rate back to baseline, <1.2s  tail errors trending down. Customers reporting reduced retry rates.

mina: excellent. Anika — I need you to take next shift for on-call followup in 45m. we’ll hand off with actions list.

anika: taking handoff. short summary for you: mitigation applied (continuous_batch_size=8, eviction_multiplier=1.5, manual evictions on node-ima-4/7), rollback PR open, canary guard added, customer comms sent. I’ll monitor for 3h and escalate if we see re-growth.

mina: thanks. items to include in postmortem: timeline, diff of scheduler change, telemetry gaps (no per-tenant metadata alert), add alert: metadata_bytes growth > 2x in 5m, and add automated guard to throttle continuous batching when metadata_pressure > threshold. assign owners.

rob: owner for config rollback/guard: rob. owner for postmortem writeup + customer impact: carla. owner for longterm block sizing and eviction policy redesign: srikar.

anika: noted. I’ll update the oncall runbook with the emergency commands and the rollback PR link.

mina: one more ask — collect heap profiles and block-manager logs for node-ima-{4,7} from 1719823000..1719824200 and attach to the postmortem.

rob: grabbing logs and heap profiles now. uploading to /artifacts/incidents/1719823456/ 

carla: CSMs acknowledged. informing top 3 affected accounts that we applied a mitigation and will follow up with root cause and ETA.

anika: monitoring looks stable for the last 6m. switching active alert thresholds: +10% to reduce noisy paging alerts while we tune.

mina: thanks team. handoff complete. please keep the thread for updates only. we’ll convert to postmortem template once data collected. :thumbsup:

srikar: quick note for followups: evaluate changing eviction policy to hybrid LFU/LRU with metadata-weighted scoring, and consider block size experiment (512KB vs 1MB) in staging.

carla: creating follow-up tickets: PMT-1292 (postmortem), INF-3334 (eviction redesign), INF-3335 (block-size experiments).

incident-bot: Incident auto-close check scheduled in 6h; manual close recommended after postmortem.

anika: acknowledged, will own monitoring and closure.

mina: closing handoff. thanks all.
